model.proposal: Bar Iowa cities and local governments from enacting civil-rights ordinances broader than or containing different discrimination categories from state law.
model.claimed_authority: Iowa General Assembly legislative authority over the Iowa Civil Rights Act and local-government ordinance authority.
model.baseline: Local governments had broader gender-identity protections in 13 cities plus unincorporated Johnson County according to the corrected source pass.
model.required_instrument: SF 579 as amended in the 2026 House session with preemption language derived from a separate proposal.
implementation_chain: SF 579 began in 2025 as a procedural civil-rights-complaint bill
preemption language was added in the 2026 House session
Governor signed March 10, 2026 according to the source pass
observed_evidence: P25-IA-01 dossier gives the preemption clause, legislative-history correction, signature date, and locality-count correction
jurisdictional_variation: Iowa used a procedural-bill amendment vehicle rather than the same legislative vehicle as Tennessee or Arkansas
response_pathways: federal Title VII protection remains separately available according to the Iowa dossier
timing_dependencies: preemption follows Iowa's 2025 removal of gender identity from the state protected-class baseline
unresolved_questions: complete enrolled SF 579 text has not been independently reviewed line by line
litigation status is not established from a retrieved filing or opinion

relationships.evidence_note: The family dossier treats Tennessee and Iowa as reuse of a similar state-local preemption mechanism across different times and legislative vehicles, not as proof of coordination.
The family dossier treats Arkansas and Iowa as structurally similar state-local preemption mechanisms without asserting a causal chain.
North Carolina is preserved as a historical member whose preemption expired, demonstrating that family membership does not imply identical current state.
Texas uses a broad preemption statute later applied in litigation to an LGBTQ ordinance; the source explicitly distinguishes this vehicle from Iowa's legislation.
